summary: Created a 512 MiB LUKS-encrypted ext3 volume on node1, automatically unlocked and mounted read-write at /srv/secure during boot. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were preserved. A full node restart confirmed persistence and data recovery.
actions_performed: Generated a root-only encryption key on node1.
Configured /etc/crypttab for automatic unlocking and /etc/fstab for mounting at /srv/secure.
Restarted node1 and verified the boot identity changed.
Verified the encrypted volume remounted automatically, retained existing data, and accepted new writes after restart.

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume is active and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: cryptsetup reports an active AES-CBC-ESSIV LUKS mapping; /dev/mapper/secure is mounted read-write as ext3 at /srv/secure.

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot
evidence.summary: crypttab and fstab contain the persistent configuration, and post-restart evidence shows the mapping and mount recovered automatically.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Both before and after restart, the system reports Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.

Healthy baseline boot ID 30180b26-a8e5-4ae3-838c-0a5b367bd3e9 was captured, reboot acknowledged, and boot ID changed to 932f2b30-6ecf-4c04-87a7-8a119979657a. The LUKS mapping, mount, retained marker, and post-restart write all succeeded.
